cities.base: Connaught Place or a hotel near New Delhi station, central for both Old and New Delhi sights
cities.name: Delhi

cities.base: a hotel near the Taj East or West Gate, close enough to walk in for sunrise
cities.name: Agra

cities.base: a hotel near the old city walls, walking distance to City Palace and Jantar Mantar
cities.name: Jaipur

places.name: Humayun's Tomb
places.note: Less crowded than the Taj and a good warm-up for Mughal architecture before Agra.

places.name: Qutub Minar
places.note: Same era as Humayun's Tomb, skip if day 2 is already full, you don't need both.

places.name: Jama Masjid
places.note: Free to enter, small camera fee, pairs with the Chandni Chowk food walk right outside.

places.name: Chandni Chowk food walk
places.note: The best meal density in Delhi, go hungry and eat your way through.

places.name: Agra Fort
places.note: The fort's view of the Taj across the river is worth it alone, don't skip thinking the Taj itself is enough.

places.name: Taj Mahal
places.note: Sunrise entry is not optional, by 9am it's a crowd and a heat problem March through October.

places.name: Amber Fort
places.note: Walk up and skip the elephant ride, it's a short queue and an animal welfare mess.

places.name: City Palace
places.note: Pairs easily with Jantar Mantar next door on the same afternoon.

places.name: Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk food walk
places.note: Mosque entry is free, small camera fee. Go hungry: parathe wali gali, jalebis at Old Famous, and butter chicken at Karim's are all within walking distance.

places.name: Red Fort
places.note: Closed Mondays. Interiors are more picked-over than the exterior suggests, but it anchors Old Delhi and pairs naturally with Jama Masjid across the road.

places.name: India Gate
places.note: War memorial arch, best at dusk when the lawns fill with families and the fountains run. Nothing to do here beyond a walk, which is the point.

places.name: Lodhi Garden
places.note: 15th century tombs scattered through a park locals actually use for jogging and picnics. Good slow morning if day 7 is more recovery than sightseeing.

places.name: Akshardham Temple
places.note: Genuinely impressive carving, and entry is free, but the exhibitions cost 260 rupees and the water show 110 more. Phones, cameras and bags are not allowed (free cloakroom), security is slow, last entry is 18:30 and it is closed Mondays.

places.name: Connaught Place
places.note: Colonial-era circular arcade of shops, cafes and bars. Useful as a normal, air-conditioned break from monuments on the buffer day.

places.name: Karim's
places.note: Old Mughlai kitchen near Jama Masjid running since 1913. Mutton korma and seekh kebabs are the reason to go, not the seating, which is basic.

places.name: Bukhara, ITC Maurya
places.note: One of Delhi's best known tandoor kitchens, dal bukhara and black lentils cooked overnight are the signature. Book ahead, it fills with both tourists and Delhi regulars.

places.name: National Museum
places.note: Good rainy-day or pollution-day fallback, Harappan seals through Mughal miniatures under one roof. Closed Mondays, and the labeling is inconsistent gallery to gallery.

places.name: Dilli Haat
places.note: Open-air crafts market with stalls rotating by state, small entry fee keeps out the worst hassle. Good for last-day souvenir shopping without haggling in Old Delhi heat.

places.name: Mehtab Bagh
places.note: Garden directly across the river from the Taj, best for sunset silhouette shots without fighting the crowd inside the complex.

places.name: Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
places.note: Marble tomb that predates and arguably inspired the Taj's inlay work, usually near empty. Skip if you only have the afternoon in Agra, keep it if you have a spare hour.

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri
places.note: The abandoned Mughal capital is genuinely impressive but it is a 3+ hour round trip you do not have on this itinerary, already flagged as a cut.

places.name: Sadar Bazaar
places.note: Ordinary market street for leather goods, marble souvenirs, and a look at Agra that isn't fort walls, easy stop between the fort and dinner.

places.name: Pinch of Spice
places.note: Reliable North Indian restaurant popular with tour groups, good butter chicken and dal, nothing fancy but consistent after a long day.

places.name: Esphahan, The Oberoi Amarvilas
places.note: Splurge dinner inside the Amarvilas with a Taj view from the terrace, book ahead, this is the one expensive meal worth the price on this leg of the trip.

places.name: Taj Nature Walk
places.note: Quiet park with a distant Taj view through the trees, good for an early walk if you want movement before the heat without the fort crowds.

places.name: Kinari Bazaar
places.note: Narrow, chaotic old city market near Jama Masjid Agra, good for street snacks and a break from the monument circuit, not set up for tourists so expect no English menus.

places.name: Jama Masjid, Agra
places.note: Small red sandstone mosque near the fort and Kinari Bazaar, quick stop if you're already in the old city, not worth a special trip on its own.

places.name: Mankameshwar Temple
places.note: Working Shiva temple near the river, small and local, worth a look only if you're passing on foot between the fort and the old city, not a destination by itself.

places.name: City Palace, Jaipur
places.note: Still partly a royal residence, textile and armor collections are decent. The Royal Grandeur ticket adds private apartments but isn't necessary for a two-day stop.

places.name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
places.note: UNESCO-listed 18th century observatory, giant stone instruments still tell time accurately. A guide helps, otherwise it's just big shapes in the sun for 20 minutes.

places.name: Hawa Mahal
places.note: The facade is the whole point, best seen and photographed from the street or a rooftop cafe across the road. Interior is skippable, not worth the ticket queue.

places.name: Johari Bazaar
places.note: Jaipur's jewelry and gem market, real trade happening not just tourist stalls. Bargain hard, don't buy 'investment' gems on a salesman's word.

places.name: Bapu Bazaar
places.note: Textiles, juttis, and block-print fabric, good for gifts. Less aggressive selling than Johari Bazaar.

places.name: Nahargarh Fort
places.note: Sits above the city, best reason to go up is the sunset view over Jaipur, not the fort interior itself. Padao Restaurant terrace inside is the spot for a drink at that hour.

places.name: Jal Mahal
places.note: Photographed from the road on the way to Amber Fort, you can't go inside. Worth a five minute stop, not a dedicated visit.

places.name: Chokhi Dhani
places.note: Village-themed dinner and entertainment complex, unapologetically touristy but the unlimited thali is genuinely good and kids like the puppet shows and camel rides. Twenty minutes outside the city so plan the drive back.

places.name: Suvarna Mahal, Rambagh Palace
places.note: Formal dining room in a former Maharaja's palace hotel, good for one splurge dinner. Book ahead, dress code enforced.

places.name: Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB)
places.note: Institution since the 1950s, purely vegetarian Rajasthani thali and sweets. Convenient lunch stop between Johari and Bapu Bazaar.

places.name: Panna Meena ka Kund
places.note: Small symmetrical stepwell a short walk from Amber Fort, good five minute detour on the way up or down, photographs well with almost no crowd compared to the fort itself.

places.name: Moti Mahal, Daryaganj
places.note: The Daryaganj branch of the Moti Mahal chain, for tandoori and Mughlai dishes; about 1,100 rupees for two on an undated listing, open daily 12:00 to midnight.

places.name: Sita Ram Diwan Chand
places.note: A chole bhature institution in Paharganj, about 200 rupees for two on an undated listing; breakfast and lunch only, listed 08:00 to 17:30, so do not plan dinner here.

places.name: Saravana Bhavan, Connaught Place
places.note: South Indian vegetarian chain on Connaught Circle, handy with Jantar Mantar; dosas and thalis for about 700 rupees for two on an undated listing, open daily 08:00 to 23:00.

places.name: Gandhi Smriti
places.note: Birla House, where Gandhi spent his last 144 days and was shot on 30 January 1948; his room is kept as it was. Free, with free guides, an hour, closed Mondays.

places.name: Indira Gandhi Memorial Museum
places.note: Indira Gandhi's home, with the spot in the garden where she was assassinated in 1984; free, an hour, 09:30 to 16:45, closed Mondays. Pairs with Gandhi Smriti a short ride away.

places.name: National Gallery of Modern Art
places.note: Founded in 1954 in Jaipur House by India Gate, with Amrita Sher-Gil, Tagore and Ravi Varma; free guided tours, two hours, closed Mondays, and check the price at the door.

places.name: National Crafts Museum and Hastkala Academy
places.note: More than 35,000 craft pieces in a village-style complex, with the Lota Cafe on site; free according to visitors, so check, 90 minutes, closed Mondays.

places.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan Museum
places.note: Opened in 2014: gifts from world leaders and the presidential cars, with only the first phase open in 2026. Book online ahead and bring photo ID, closed Mondays, and check the price.

places.name: National Rail Museum
places.note: Locomotives from 1855 on, including the Fairy Queen, plus a toy train round the grounds; two hours, 10:00 to 17:00, closed Mondays, and check the price.

places.name: Purana Qila
places.note: The fort Humayun began in 1533, with Sher Shah's Qila-i-Kuhna mosque of 1541 and the Sher Mandal; an hour, 07:00 to 17:00, a boating lake and a sound and light show. Check the price for foreigners.

places.name: Archaeological Museum, Purana Qila
places.note: A small 1973 museum of finds from the fort digs, Mauryan to early Mughal, on the fort ticket; 30 minutes, check the price, and it has closed for renovation before, so check it is open.

places.name: Jantar Mantar, Delhi
places.note: Jai Singh II's 1724 observatory of 13 masonry instruments, a short walk from Connaught Place; 45 minutes, 09:00 to 18:00, cheaper booked online, and check the price for foreigners.

places.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
places.note: The Sikh shrine tied to Guru Har Krishan, with a sarovar whose water is held to heal; open 24 hours, free, and the langar meal is free too. Cover your head, and photography is restricted.

places.name: Safdarjung Tomb
places.note: Built in 1754 for Safdarjung, the last Mughal garden tomb in Delhi and a quiet end to the line that starts at Humayun's Tomb; 45 minutes, 09:00 to 19:00, and check the price for foreigners.

places.name: Desi Vibes
places.note: North Indian dining room on Fatehabad Road opposite the Trident, rated 4.9 on Google; about 1,200 rupees for two on an undated listing, open daily 12:00 to 22:45.

places.name: Karchi
places.note: A local restaurant in Kamla Nagar, about 7 km north of the Taj, so it suits a dinner on the way to or from Sikandra; about 600 rupees for two on an undated listing, open daily 12:30 to 23:30.

places.name: Shahen Shah, Hotel Grand Imperial
places.note: The restaurant of the Hotel Grand Imperial on MG Road, near Agra Fort; about 2,000 rupees for two on an undated listing with no reviews yet, so check, open daily 07:00 to 22:00.

places.name: Tomb of Akbar, Sikandra
places.note: Begun by Akbar and finished by Jahangir in 1605 to 1613, five tiers of red sandstone and marble in a charbagh with deer; an hour, 06:00 to 18:00, and check the price.

places.name: Tomb of Mariam-uz-Zamani
places.note: Built by Jahangir in 1627 for his mother, a Mughal and Rajput blend about 1 km from Akbar's Tomb and almost always empty; 20 minutes, and check the price for foreigners.

places.name: Taj Museum
places.note: Plans and drawings of the Taj, Mughal miniatures and Shah Jahan's plate said to detect poison; free with a Taj ticket according to visitors, 30 minutes, closed Fridays.

places.name: Chini Ka Rauza
places.note: The 1630s tomb of Afzal Khan, the one building in Agra faced in glazed Persian tiles, near the Baby Taj; poorly kept, 25 minutes, and check the price.

places.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
places.note: The pyaaz kachori and sweet shop on Station Road that Jaipur sends visitors to; about 750 rupees for two on the current listing, open daily 06:00 to 22:30, best for breakfast.

places.name: Handi Restaurant, MI Road
places.note: A long-running MI Road restaurant rated 4.1 on Google from 13,000 ratings, about 1,200 rupees for two; open 12:00 to 15:30 and 18:00 to 23:00 daily.

places.name: Niros
places.note: An old MI Road dining room at Panch Batti, about 1,700 rupees for two on the current listing; open 11:00 to 16:00 and 18:00 to 23:00 daily.

places.name: Indian Coffee House, MI Road
places.note: Coffee, dosas and snacks for about 200 rupees for two, a cheap stop rather than a full meal, open daily 08:00 to 21:00; there are no ratings on the listing, so check.

places.name: Albert Hall Museum
places.note: Swinton Jacob's Indo-Saracenic hall, opened in 1887, with an Egyptian mummy, coins and arms; 90 minutes, open to 20:00 and lit up after dark, and check the price.

places.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
places.note: Block printing in a restored 400-year-old haveli in Amer, with live demonstrations; easy after Amber Fort, 90 minutes, Sunday 11:00 to 16:30, closed Mondays, and check the price.

places.name: Jawahar Kala Kendra
places.note: Charles Correa's 1986 arts centre, laid out as a nine-square mandala that mirrors the old city grid; an hour, 09:00 to 21:00, and check the price for shows.

places.name: Jaigarh Fort
places.note: Sawai Jai Singh II's 18th century fort above Amber, home of the Jaivana, once the largest cannon on wheels; two hours, 09:00 to 18:30, and check the price.

outings.why: A full day on foot covering Mughal-era Old Delhi and colonial New Delhi, 6-7 hours and worth pacing yourself for.
outings.name: Old Delhi and New Delhi sights

outings.why: Free mosque entry aside from a small camera fee, then a street food crawl that's the best meal density in the city, go hungry.
outings.name: Jama Masjid and Chandni Chowk food walk

outings.why: Don't skip this thinking the Taj is enough, the fort's view of the Taj across the river is worth it alone.
outings.name: Agra Fort visit

outings.why: Gates open around 6am and sunrise entry is not optional, by 9am it's a crowd and a heat problem March through October.
outings.name: Taj Mahal at sunrise

outings.why: Walk up rather than take the elephant ride, it's a short queue and an animal welfare mess.
outings.name: Amber Fort morning

outings.why: Afternoon after Amber Fort, the Palace and the observatory are close together in the old city.
outings.name: City Palace and Jantar Mantar

outings.why: A half day of bazaars with the Hawa Mahal seen from outside only, before the afternoon drive or flight back to Delhi.
outings.name: Jaipur old city bazaars and Hawa Mahal

destination.name: Golden Triangle: Delhi, Agra, Jaipur
destination.pitch: Seven nights of Delhi, Agra and Jaipur done properly by car, the Taj at sunrise and two Mughal capitals either side, not a relaxing trip but a complete one.
destination.caveat: This is a car-and-guide trip through pollution and traffic, not a relaxing one, and it gives you neither beaches nor mountains. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Old and New Delhi and Jaipur's old city give you dense, chaotic, functioning Indian urban life, not a museum version of it.
because.food: Chandni Chowk alone is the best meal density of the trip, a serious street food crawl for under 10 USD.
because.culture: Three Mughal capitals back to back, forts, tombs and the Taj itself, with almost no filler.
